hook.line: Every office has its own way of deciding who goes first. *Por orden de* names the rule, and you will see it on every sign and agenda.
hook.es: Se atiende por orden de llegada.
hook.en: People are served in order of arrival.

examples.es: Se atiende por orden de llegada.
examples.en: People are served in order of arrival.

examples.es: Los temas se tratarán por orden de prioridad.
examples.en: The topics will be dealt with in order of priority.

examples.es: Los estudiantes pasan por orden de lista.
examples.en: The students go up in the order of the roll.

examples.es: Los socios aparecen por orden alfabético.
examples.en: The members are listed in alphabetical order.

examples.es: ¿Se atiende por orden de llegada o con cita?
examples.en: Are people served in order of arrival or by appointment?

examples.es: Las respuestas se enviarán por orden de inscripción.
examples.en: The answers will be sent in order of registration.

rule:
*Por orden de* plus the criterion says what decides the order: *llegada* (arrival), *prioridad*, *lista*, *inscripción*.

No article after *de*: *por orden de llegada*, not *de la llegada*.

For the alphabet and similar, the adjective comes straight after: *por orden alfabético*, *cronológico*.

It is often paired with *se*: *se atiende*, *se tratarán*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a fixed phrase. The thing after *de* is a bare noun, like a label.

People are served by order of the boss.
People are served on arrival day.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: People are served in order of arrival.
yourTurn.answer: Se atiende por orden de llegada.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *de edad* or *de la edad* and type the whole sentence: *Entran por orden ___.*
yourTurn.why: The criterion after *por orden* takes no article.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The topics will be dealt with in order of priority.
yourTurn.answer: Los temas se tratarán por orden de prioridad.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The members are listed in alphabetical order.
yourTurn.answer: Los socios aparecen por orden alfabético.
yourTurn.why: For the alphabet, the adjective follows *orden* directly.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a question: *Se atiende por orden de llegada.* Say: Are people served in order of arrival or by appointment?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Se atiende por orden de llegada o con cita?
yourTurn.why: Add *o con cita* for the alternative.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The answers will be sent in order of registration.
yourTurn.answer: Las respuestas se enviarán por orden de inscripción.
yourTurn.why: *Se enviarán* is plural because *respuestas* is plural.

pitfalls.wrong: Se atiende por orden de la llegada.
pitfalls.right: Se atiende por orden de llegada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *por orden de* the criterion stays bare, with no *la*.

pitfalls.wrong: Se atiende en orden de llegada.
pitfalls.right: Se atiende por orden de llegada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase uses *por*, not *en*.

pitfalls.right: Se atiende por orden de llegada.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You need *de* before the criterion.

personal: Say how something works at your work, school or favourite place, using *por orden de*.
